mise installs the development tools your projects need, sets        ▄▄  ▄▄▄  ▄▄
their environment variables, and runs their tasks.                 ▟  ▙▟   ▙▟  ▙
                                                                   ▜▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▛
You declare tools, environment variables, and tasks in              ▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀
mise.toml. `mise use <TOOL>` installs a tool and adds it to the      ▗▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▖
project's mise.toml, `mise install` installs everything the          ▌ ▀   ▔ ▐
config requests, and `mise run <TASK>` runs a task. Docs:            ▝▄ ▀▄▀ ▄▘
https://mise.jdx.dev

Usage: mise [FLAGS] [TASK] [SUBCOMMAND]

Commands:
  activate      Print the script to activate mise in an
                interactive shell
  backends      Manage backends [aliases: b, backend,
                backend-list]
  bin-paths     List the bin directories of the active tools
  bootstrap     Set up this machine from your mise config
                [aliases: bs]
  cache         Manage the mise cache
  completion    Generate shell completions [aliases: complete,
                completions]
  config        Manage config files [aliases: cfg, toml]
  daemons       [experimental] Manage project daemons with
                pitchfork [aliases: daemon]
  deactivate    Print the script to disable mise in the current
                shell session
  deps          [experimental] Manage project dependencies
                [aliases: dep, prepare]
  doctor        Check your mise setup for problems [aliases: dr]
  dotfiles      Deploy, track, and sync dotfiles [aliases: dot]
  edit          Edit mise.toml interactively
  en            Start a subshell with mise's tools and
                environment
  env           Print the environment for the current
                configuration [aliases: e]
  exec          Run a command with mise's tools and environment
                [aliases: x]
  fmt           Format mise TOML configuration
  generate      Generate project files such as CI workflows, git
                hooks, and scripts [aliases: gen, g]
  implode       Remove the mise CLI and all related data
  install       Install the tools in your config, or specific
                tool versions [aliases: i]
  install-into  Install a tool version into a directory outside
                mise
  installs      [experimental] Inspect and choose
                identity-layout installations
  latest        Print the latest version that matches a version
                request
  link          Symlink a tool version into mise [aliases: ln]
  lock          Create or refresh lockfile versions, checksums,
                and download URLs
  ls            List installed and active tool versions
                [aliases: list]
  ls-remote     List tool versions available to install
                [aliases: list-all, list-remote]
  lsp           Run the language server for mise config files
                over stdin/stdout
  mcp           Run the Model Context Protocol server over
                stdin/stdout
  oci           [experimental] Build, push, and run OCI images
                of a project's tools
  outdated      Show outdated tool versions
  packslip      Inspect and reset the signers mise has pinned
                for packslip tools
  patrons       Show the individuals supporting mise as
                Patron-tier members
  plugins       Manage plugins [aliases: p, plugin, plugin-list]
  prune         Delete tool versions that nothing uses
  registry      List registry shorthand names and their backends
  reshim        Create shims for executables provided by
                installed tools
  run           Run tasks and their dependencies [aliases: r]
  search        Search for available tools
  secrets       [experimental] Inspect the project's secrets
                source
  self-update   Update mise itself
  set           Set, show, or list environment variables in
                mise.toml [aliases: ev, env-vars]
  settings      Manage settings
  shell         Set a tool version for the current shell session
                [aliases: sh]
  shell-alias   Manage shell aliases
  skills        List and link the agent skills that active tools
                ship [aliases: skill]
  sponsors      Show the companies sponsoring mise and the
                jdx.dev open source tools
  ssh           Open an SSH session, optionally borrowing
                read-only GitHub access
  sync          Use tool versions installed by other version
                managers
  tasks         Manage tasks [aliases: t, task]
  test-tool     Test that a tool installs and runs
  token         Show which Git provider token mise uses
  tool          Show information about a tool
  tool-alias    Manage tool backend and version aliases
                [aliases: alias, aliases]
  tool-stub     Run a tool stub file
  trust         Mark a config file as trusted
  uninstall     Remove installed tool versions
  unset         Remove environment variables from mise.toml
  untrust       Remove explicit trust for a config
  unuse         Remove tool requests from config files and prune
                unused installations [aliases: rm, remove]
  upgrade       Upgrade outdated tools [aliases: up]
  use           Install a tool and add it to configuration
                [aliases: u]
  vars          List, set, and ask for config vars
  version       Show the version of mise [aliases: v]
  watch         Run tasks and rerun them when files change
                [aliases: w]
  where         Show the install directory of a tool version
  which         Show the path a tool's executable resolves to
  help          Print this message or the help of the given
                subcommand(s)

Arguments:
  [TASK]  Task to run

          Shorthand for `mise run <TASK>`.

Flags:
  -C, --cd <DIR>     Run as if mise were started in DIR
  -E, --env <ENV>    Load the `mise.<ENV>.toml` config files
                     (same as MISE_ENV)

                     Repeat the flag or separate names with
                     commas to load several environments.
  -j, --jobs <JOBS>  How many jobs to run in parallel; defaults
                     to the `jobs` setting

                     Values below 1 are treated as 1.
                     [env: MISE_JOBS]
  -q, --quiet        Suppress non-error messages
                     [env: MISE_QUIET]
  -v, --verbose      Show extra output (use -vv for even more)
  -y, --yes          Answer yes to all confirmation prompts
      --no-config    Do not load any config files

                     Same as `MISE_NO_CONFIG=1`.
      --no-env       Do not load environment variables from
                     config files

                     Same as `MISE_NO_ENV=1`.
      --no-hooks     Do not run hooks from config files

                     Same as `MISE_NO_HOOKS=1`.
      --raw          Connect tasks and install commands directly
                     to the terminal

                     Commands then run one at a time. Same as
                     `MISE_RAW=1` or the `raw` setting.
      --locked       Require download URLs from the lockfile
                     when installing

                     Installing fails when the lockfile has no
                     pre-resolved URL for a tool on the current
                     platform, so mise does not call the GitHub
                     or aqua registry APIs to find one. Same as
                     `MISE_LOCKED=1` or the `locked` setting.
      --silent       Suppress all task output and mise non-error
                     messages
  -h, --help         Print help

Examples:
    Install node 24 and add it to the project's mise.toml
    $ mise use node@24

    Make node 24 your global default
    $ mise use -g node@24

    Install every tool the config requests
    $ mise install

    Run a command with the project's tools on PATH
    $ mise x -- npm install

    Run a command with a tool that is not in the config
    $ mise x python@3.13 -- python app.py

    Add an environment variable to mise.toml
    $ mise set NODE_ENV=production

    Run the build task
    $ mise run build

    Rerun the build task when its sources change
    $ mise watch build

    Choose tools to upgrade from a menu
    $ mise upgrade --interactive

    Turn off color in the global config
    $ mise settings color=0

Author: Jeff Dickey <@jdx>

Manage tasks

With no subcommand, lists tasks like `mise tasks ls` and accepts the same flags.
With a task name, shows that task like `mise tasks info`. To run a task, use
`mise run`.

Usage: mise tasks [FLAGS] [TASK] [SUBCOMMAND]

Commands:
  add       Add a task
  deps      Show the dependency tree of tasks
  edit      Open a task in your editor
  graph     Show the monorepo project graph
  info      Show a task's definition
  ls        List available tasks
  rm        Remove tasks [aliases: remove]
  set       Change fields of an existing TOML task
  validate  Check task definitions for errors
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Arguments:
  [TASK]  Task to show, as `mise tasks info` does

Flags:
  -g, --global                   Only show global tasks
  -J, --json                     Output in JSON format
  -l, --local                    Deprecated alias for --no-global

                                 Removed in mise 2027.7.0.
      --no-global                Only show non-global tasks
  -x, --extended                 Show all columns
  -a, --all                      Include tasks from every project in the
                                 monorepo, not only the current directory's
                                 hierarchy
      --hidden                   Show hidden tasks
      --name-only                Print only task names, one per line (for fzf
                                 and similar tools)
      --no-header                Do not print the table header
      --sort <COLUMN>            Column to sort by (default: name)
                                 [possible values: name, alias, description,
                                 source]
      --sort-order <SORT_ORDER>  Sort direction (default: asc)
                                 [possible values: asc, desc]
  -h, --help                     Print help

Global flags:
  -C, --cd <DIR>                 Run as if mise were started in DIR
  -E, --env <ENV>                Load the `mise.<ENV>.toml` config files (same
                                 as MISE_ENV)

                                 Repeat the flag or separate names with commas
                                 to load several environments.
  -j, --jobs <JOBS>              How many jobs to run in parallel; defaults to
                                 the `jobs` setting

                                 Values below 1 are treated as 1.
                                 [env: MISE_JOBS]
  -q, --quiet                    Suppress non-error messages
                                 [env: MISE_QUIET]
  -v, --verbose                  Show extra output (use -vv for even more)
  -y, --yes                      Answer yes to all confirmation prompts
      --raw                      Connect tasks and install commands directly to
                                 the terminal

                                 Commands then run one at a time. Same as
                                 `MISE_RAW=1` or the `raw` setting.
      --locked                   Require download URLs from the lockfile when
                                 installing

                                 Installing fails when the lockfile has no
                                 pre-resolved URL for a tool on the current
                                 platform, so mise does not call the GitHub or
                                 aqua registry APIs to find one. Same as
                                 `MISE_LOCKED=1` or the `locked` setting.
      --silent                   Suppress all task output and mise non-error
                                 messages

Examples:
    List tasks
    $ mise tasks

    Show the build task
    $ mise tasks build

    Include hidden tasks, sorted by source
    $ mise tasks --hidden --sort source
